correctness.rationale: With the explicitly added vacuous score of 1 at R=0, the published one-cohesive definitions reduce to containment or coverage of each cohesive candidate's full supporter set. Every one-cohesive subgroup lies in at least one such set, and the full set is itself cohesive. Independent approval columns give R~Bin(m,q_n), with the integer threshold correctly rounded up. For each ordered pair (c,W) with c omitted, the no-witness probability is (1-p(1-p)^k)^n. The union bound is over exactly m*binom(m-1,k) pairs. Its complement forbids all omitted candidates from receiving either type of credit simultaneously, while elected cohesive candidates always receive credit. This proves the optimizer statement on that event, the deterministic lower bounds even outside it, and both score errors by bounding the exceptional probability. The standardized threshold tends to -theta/sqrt((1/k)(1-1/k)); the ceiling contributes O(1/sqrt(n)) and the separation error decays exponentially for fixed m,k. The fixed-p limits and exceptional p=1 case also follow. Exact summation confirms 93/256 and 55133/71680. The supplied files were inspected without running the uploaded script; small independent enumerations corroborate finite cases but are not the proof. The reference to Definitions 2–8 should be read as including Proposition 7, which states the SJR score-one equivalence.
